question: How to design for manufacture and assembly (DfMA) using robotics?

answer.answer:
To design for manufacture and assembly with robots, standardise first: highly standardised components (AT7) is the single requirement that feeds both the DfMA process (PR9) and robotic assembly (PR4), and it is the most widely drawn on of DfMA's four cited requirements, the others being a modular product architecture (AT2), early contractor involvement (CO11) and a parametric/computational algorithm and machine-code base (RE1). None of those four is a machine: three are design or organisational properties and the fourth is code, so the robot is not what DfMA requires, standardisation is. On the robotics side the record is thinner than the literature: a robotic arm (RE2) is the only machine cited as a requirement of robotic assembly, path-planning (PR12) is cited as enabling it but carried by only 2 of the 50 coded cases, and the mobile factory (CO12) is a direct cited precondition carried by none of the 50. Downstream, DfMA orients you to prefabrication/off-site (PR2) and modularisation (PR5), and the measured gains in time, quality and safety attach to prefabrication rather than to the robot; expect a heavy human load throughout, since significant human involvement (RE6) is drawn on by all 50 cases and workforce training (RI6) by 44.

**What DfMA requires.** PR9 "DfMA for DFAB process" (Process) is drawn on by 15 of the 50 coded cases and carries 3 inbound and 3 outbound cited edges [1]. Its requirements, reading each relation rather than its direction: AT7 "Highly standardised" enablesCapability PR9, because design standardisation and simplification is a DfMA enabler for offsite construction, carried by 13 of the 50 [1]; AT2 "Modular" enablesCapability PR9, on the alignment of product and process modularity, carried by 7 [1]; CO11 "Early contractor involvement" enablesCapability PR9, early collaboration being among the DfMA enablers, carried by 11 [1]; and PR9 dependsOn RE1 "Parametric/computational/data-driven algorithm/machine code", the DfMA-oriented process combining DfMA with BIM parametric design, carried by 8 [1]. These are not four equal requirements: 25 of the 50 cases draw on AT7 [1], against 14 for CO11 [1], 12 for AT2 [1] and 11 for RE1 [1]. All four edges are peer-reviewed. Standardisation and modularity also reinforce each other in both directions: AT7 enablesCapability AT2 (carried by 11) [1] and AT2 enablesCapability AT7 (carried by 11) [1], while bespoke/customised design (AT1) constrains AT2, carried by 4 [1], which is the trade-off to design against.

**What DfMA produces.** PR9 enablesCapability PR2 "Prefabrication/off-site", orienting the project toward offsite manufacture, carried by 15 of the 50 [1], and PR9 enablesCapability PR5 "Modularisation", carried by 8 [1]; PR5 in turn enables mass-customisation (PR11, carried by 8) and opens entry to specialised suppliers and manufacturers (AC13, carried by 10) [1]. The value edges in this material hang off prefabrication, not off the robot: PR2 enables VA2 "Reduce time/improve productivity/efficiency" (19) [1], VA3 "Improve quality/performance" (18) [1], VA10 "Reduce errors/constraints" (14) [1] and VA13 "Improve site safety" (12) [1], at the price of a dependency on precise up-front planning and logistics (RI14, carried by 18) [1] and on regulatory and certification arrangements for offsite compliance (RI18, carried by 10) [1].

**Where robotics attaches.** PR4 "Robotic assembly" (Process) is drawn on by 13 of the 50 and carries 4 inbound and 6 outbound edges, all listed [1], so its requirement set can be quoted as complete: RE2 "Robotic arm" (both as enablesCapability and as dependsOn, carried by 12) [1], AT7 "Highly standardised", on Japanese automated erection systems relying on standardised prefabricated components, carried by 10 [1], PR2 as a precondition, automated overhead delivery and assembly requiring extensive prefabrication and unification of materials, carried by 4 [1], PR12 "Path-planning", carried by 2 [1], and CO12 "Mobile factory" (Condition), carried by 0 [1]. AT7 is therefore the join: it is the only enabler cited into both PR9 and PR4, which is the practical instruction, standardise the component set and the interfaces and both the DfMA process and the robot follow. The two weak edges are worth stating outright: 26 of the 50 cases draw on PR12 [1] and 1 on CO12 [1], yet as cited preconditions of robotic assembly they are exhibited by 2 and 0 cases respectively, so both are asserted in the literature far more firmly than the coded record carries them. On the return side, PR4 amplifies VA2, carried by 13 [1], amplifies VA6 "Reduce cost", carried by 7 [1], enables VA10 "Reduce errors/constraints", carried by only 1 [1], and dependsOn RI12 "Delivery/business model/work culture", carried by 2 [1], the last being the reminder that robotics adoption rests on organisational context.

**What edge-walking misses.** Two robotic enablers in scope carry no cited edge at all and are visible only through how many cases draw on them: PR15 "Robotic pickup/selection" (Process), 19 of the 50, no dependency edges [1], and RE10 "Gantry-type robotic system" (Resource), 5 of the 50, no dependency edges [1]; the retrieved material does not cover unmanned mobile vehicles, so this answer says nothing about them. The same applies to the human and process side: RE6 "Significant human involvement" is drawn on by 50 of the 50 and has no edge [1], RI8 "Rely on DFAB technology" by 45 with none [1], RI7 "Rely on DFAB specialist" by 23 with none [1], and the two process styles split evenly, 19 of the 50 on AT11 "Sequential design-DFAB process" [1] against 19 on AT12 "Integrated design-DFAB process" [1], the latter fed by vertical integration (CO10, carried by 14) [1], early contractor involvement (CO11, carried by 10) [1] and a DFAB design coordinator (AC4, carried by 7) [1]. The cited dependency layer is sparse, 100 edges touching 68 of the 140 enablers, which is a property of the literature and not of the record [1], so treat the absence of an edge as an unconnected claim, not an unimportant enabler.

**Evidence limit.** Every claim above rests on the cited literature layer and on how many of the 50 coded cases draw on each enabler. The retrieved material carries no deployed Process RP record, no census record and no firm for DfMA with robotics, so there is no project-level account here of a company that did it, and this answer should not be read as resting on one.
